# QS-CFW-4922-70 Quality specification - gear blank CFW-4922-70 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4922-70

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance requirements for forged gear blank CFW-4922-70 (8620) produced at Plant P2. It applies to finished blanks delivered to machining and heat-treat operations and governs hardness, bore tolerance, and forging weight as produced by the forging line.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 8620 (as specified on part print) |
| Hardness (through section as produced) | The hardness range for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 38-42 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is ±0.03 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 69.8 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and scale that would affect machining (see inspection method). |

Inspection method
- Hardness: Measure hardness at representative locations specified on the part print using a calibrated Rockwell tester. Record readings and confirm they fall within the hardness range for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 38-42 HRC. Reject parts outside this range.
- Bore diameter: Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or micrometer; verify bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is ±0.03 mm relative to nominal. Record measurements on inspection record.
- Weight: Weigh each forging on calibrated scale and verify the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 69.8 kg. Overweight parts are nonconforming.
- Visual: Inspect surfaces for defects that would affect machining; document findings on the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
Parts found outside any requirement shall be segregated and tagged. Engineering disposition is required prior to release. Nonconformances shall be documented in the quality record and corrective action initiated as appropriate. Rework or scrap decisions must ensure final product meets the requirements table before release.
